title: Cost of Studying in USA for Indian Students 2026: Tuition, Living & Funding Guide
excerpt: Complete breakdown of USA study costs for Indian students: tuition by university type, living expenses by city, total annual costs in USD and INR, plus funding and work opportunities.
kw: cost of studying in USA, USA tuition fees 2026, living expenses USA, Indian students budget, study abroad funding, F-1 visa on-campus work

sections.h: How Much Does It Cost to Study in the USA in 2026?
sections.body:
The total cost of studying in the USA for Indian students ranges from USD 25,000�75,000 per year, depending on the university type, location, and lifestyle. Public universities are generally more affordable than private institutions, while living costs vary significantly by city and state. Major metropolitan areas like San Francisco, New York, and Boston are substantially more expensive than smaller college towns in the Midwest.

For most Indian students pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree, plan to spend USD 30,000�50,000 annually (approximately INR 25�40 lakhs). This comprehensive figure includes tuition, accommodation, food, transportation, health insurance, and miscellaneous expenses. A realistic first-year budget for an out-of-state public university in a medium-sized city would be approximately USD 45,000�55,000 (?36�44 lakhs).

Costs have increased by 3�5% annually over the past decade, a trend expected to continue. International students typically face higher tuition than in-state students at public universities but may receive substantial merit scholarships from private institutions. Always confirm current tuition and fees on official university websites before applying, as these figures change frequently.

sections.h: Annual Tuition Fees by University Type (2026)
sections.body: University tuition in the USA is the largest expense, varying by institution type and whether you're an international student.

callout.text: International students pay out-of-state tuition at public universities. Private universities charge the same tuition to all students, but may offer larger scholarships.

sections.h: Living Expenses: Accommodation, Food & Transport
sections.body: After tuition, living costs are the second-largest expense. These vary dramatically by city and state.
bullets: **On-campus housing**: USD 800–1,500/month (often included in package)
**Off-campus apartments**: USD 600–2,500/month depending on location
**Utilities**: USD 100–200/month (electricity, internet, water)
**Food (grocery plan)**: USD 250–400/month if cooking; USD 400–800/month on meal plans
**Transportation**: Most universities offer free/subsidized campus shuttle; public transit USD 40–150/month

sections.h: How to Fund Your USA Education: Scholarships, Loans & Aid
sections.body:
A comprehensive 2-year master's degree in the USA typically costs USD 90,000�150,000 total for public universities (USD 140,000�200,000 for private universities). Here are realistic annual and total budgets for different institution types and locations. Public universities in smaller cities offer the most affordable pathway, while private universities and major metropolitan areas significantly increase total costs.

First-generation Indian students and those from smaller hometowns should budget on the higher end to account for cultural adjustment costs, additional travel home, and unforeseen expenses. Many universities provide cost-of-living breakdowns on their websites; use these as your planning baseline. Factor in one-way flights (USD 800�1,200), initial deposits, and setup costs when arriving in the US.
steps: Apply for university-specific scholarships (many award merit aid to international students; check university websites)
Search external scholarships via Fulbright (US-based programs for Indian students), Inlaks, and nonprofit databases
Open a student education loan with Indian banks (HDFC, ICICI, Axis, SBI) covering up to 90% of education costs at competitive rates
Secure a co-signer (parent or relative) for loan approval
Apply for financial aid via FAFSA (limited for international students, but some universities have need-blind aid)
Work on-campus during studies (up to 20 hours/week on F-1 visa) to offset living costs

sections.h: On-Campus Work & Earnings (F-1 Visa Rules)
sections.body: International students on F-1 visas can work on-campus for up to 20 hours per week during the academic term and full-time during breaks, earning USD 15–20/hour at most universities.
bullets: **Work-study jobs** (library, dining hall, admin): USD 15–18/hour, ~15–20 hours/week = USD 1,200–1,400/month
**Hourly earnings**: USD 240–280/week (20 hours × $15–18/hour average)
**Annual on-campus earnings**: USD 10,000–15,000 (covering 20–30% of living costs)
**Off-campus work** (Optional Practical Training/OPT): Available after graduation on F-1 visa extension

callout.text: Combine on-campus work with a student loan to significantly reduce out-of-pocket costs. Many Indian students work 15–20 hours/week, earn USD 1,200/month, and reduce education loan burden by USD 12,000–15,000 yearly.

sections.h: Education Loans for Indian Students: Interest Rates & Repayment
sections.body: Indian banks offer education loans for US studies with interest rates between 6–10% per annum. Maximum loan amount is typically 90–100% of total education costs (tuition + living expenses for the entire program).

sections.h: Managing Your Budget: Monthly Spending Tips
sections.body: Most Indian students budget approximately USD 2,500–3,500/month for living expenses (excluding tuition). Here's a realistic monthly breakdown:
bullets: **Accommodation**: USD 800–1,500 (on-campus or shared apartment)
**Food**: USD 350–500 (cooking at home, occasional dining out)
**Utilities & Internet**: USD 100–150
**Transport**: USD 40–100 (campus shuttle or transit)
**Phone & Subscriptions**: USD 50–100
**Clothing, Entertainment, Miscellaneous**: USD 200–300
**Total**: USD 1,500–2,750/month

sections.h: Post-Graduation: OPT Earnings & H-1B Transition
sections.body:
After completing your degree, you can work in the USA for up to 12 months (or 24 months for STEM graduates) on Optional Practical Training (OPT), earning USD 50,000�80,000 annually. This significant earning potential helps many students repay their education loans relatively quickly before either transitioning to H-1B visa sponsorship or returning to India. OPT work experience is highly valued by Indian employers as well, giving you a competitive advantage in India's job market.

The combination of USA work experience and relevant educational credentials makes Indian OPT graduates highly desirable to both US and Indian employers. Many students use their OPT earnings to pay down 50�100% of their education loan within the 12�24 month work period. See our full guides on USA OPT STEM Extension 2026 and H-1B visa pathways for detailed transition strategies and timeline planning.

faqs: How much does it cost to study in the USA per year?

For Indian students, annual costs range from **USD 25,000–75,000** (₹20–60 lakhs), depending on university type and city. Public universities in smaller cities cost USD 30,000–40,000/year; private universities cost USD 55,000–70,000/year.
What is the cost of living in USA for Indian students?

Monthly living expenses (excluding tuition) range from **USD 900–3,250** depending on the city. Midwest cities (Columbus, Madison) cost USD 900–1,500/month; major cities (NYC, SF, Boston) cost USD 1,800–3,250/month.
Can I work part-time in the USA on an F-1 visa?
Yes, **F-1 visa holders can work up to 20 hours/week on-campus during studies** and full-time during breaks. On-campus jobs pay USD 15–20/hour, earning USD 10,000–15,000 annually.
What is the average tuition for international students at US universities?
Out-of-state tuition at public universities is **USD 25,000–40,000/year**. Private universities charge **USD 40,000–65,000/year**. Community colleges cost USD 8,000–15,000/year.
How can I fund my USA education as an Indian student?

Fund your education through: (1) university scholarships and merit aid, (2) external scholarships (Fulbright, Inlaks), (3) Indian education loans (SBI, HDFC, ICICI) at 7–10% interest, (4) on-campus work (20 hrs/week), (5) personal savings.
What is the interest rate for education loans from Indian banks?
Indian banks charge **6–10% per annum** for education loans. Repayment period is typically 7–15 years, with a moratorium of 6 months after completing your course.
Is it cheaper to study at public or private universities in the USA?

Public universities are significantly cheaper: **USD 25,000–40,000/year** vs. private universities at **USD 40,000–65,000/year**. However, private universities often offer larger merit scholarships to international students.
How much can I earn working on-campus at a US university?
On-campus work pays **USD 15–20/hour**. Working 20 hours/week earns approximately **USD 1,200–1,400/month or USD 10,000–15,000 annually**, covering 20–30% of living costs.

title: Cost of Studying in Canada for Indians 2026: Tuition, Living & GIC Requirements
excerpt: Complete cost breakdown for Indian students in Canada: tuition by province, living expenses, GIC requirements for study permits, PGWP eligibility, and work hour limits.
kw: cost of studying in Canada, Canada tuition fees 2026, living expenses Canada, GIC requirement Canada, study permit cost, PGWP work hours

sections.h: Total Cost of Studying in Canada for Indian Students 2026
sections.body:
The annual cost of studying in Canada for Indian students ranges from CAD 25,000�55,000 (USD 18,000�40,000 or approximately INR 20�44 lakhs), depending on the program, institution, and province. Canada is significantly cheaper than the USA or UK for international students�typically 20�30% less expensive�making it an increasingly popular choice for Indian students seeking quality education and post-study work permits (PGWP). The combination of lower tuition, affordable living costs, and the valuable Post-Graduation Work Permit (up to 3 years) makes Canada exceptional value.

For a 2-year master's degree, total costs range from CAD 50,000�110,000 (INR 30�66 lakhs). A 4-year bachelor's degree costs CAD 100,000�220,000 (INR 60�132 lakhs) total. These costs are significantly lower than USA equivalents while offering better post-graduation work permits and a clearer pathway to permanent residency through the Express Entry system. Indian students increasingly prefer Canada's clearer PR pathway and lower overall costs.

sections.h: Tuition Fees by Province & Program Level (2026)
sections.body: Canada's tuition varies by province, institution, and field of study. Engineering and business programs are typically the most expensive.

callout.text: Quebec universities (McGill, Concordia, Université de Montreal) often have lower tuition for international students compared to Ontario. Business and engineering programs are 20–30% more expensive than liberal arts.

sections.h: Living Expenses in Canada: City-by-City Breakdown
sections.body: Living costs in Canada vary by city. Smaller cities are significantly more affordable than Toronto and Vancouver.

sections.h: Study Permit & GIC (Guaranteed Investment Certificate) Requirement
sections.body:
To obtain a Canadian study permit, Indian students must demonstrate financial support through a **Guaranteed Investment Certificate (GIC)** held in a Canadian bank, or proof of funds in a Canadian bank account.

As of 2024, the GIC requirement has been removed for most countries, but International Mobility Program (IMP) and provincial requirements may still apply. Confirm current requirements on Government of Canada's official website.

rows: Proof of funds for first year
Proof of funds for entire program

callout.text: GIC and proof-of-funds requirements change frequently. Verify current Study Permit requirements on canada.ca before submitting applications. As of June 2026, many countries may have relaxed GIC requirements—confirm with your province and institution.

sections.h: Work Hours & Part-Time Earnings in Canada
sections.body: International students can work **up to 20 hours per week during the academic term** and full-time (40+ hours) during scheduled breaks (summer, winter). This significantly helps offset living costs.
bullets: **Minimum wage** (varies by province): CAD 14–16.55/hour (BC, Ontario, Alberta 2026)
**Part-time on-campus jobs**: CAD 16–20/hour (library, dining, administration)
**Off-campus retail/food service**: CAD 15–18/hour
**Monthly earnings (20 hours/week)**: CAD 1,120–1,440 (₹0.67–0.86 lakhs)
**Annual earnings (part-time + breaks)**: CAD 12,000–18,000 (₹7.2–10.8 lakhs), covering 20–30% of costs

callout.text: Unlike the USA, Canada allows off-campus work without additional permits. Many students work part-time in restaurants, retail, or tutoring to earn CAD 12,000–18,000 annually.

sections.h: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) & Pathway to Permanent Residency
sections.body:
Canada's Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) is one of the most valuable benefits for Indian students. Graduates can work legally in Canada for 1–3 years after graduation, and this work experience counts toward Canadian permanent residency (PR) applications through the Express Entry system.

See our complete guide: [Canada PGWP 2026 Guide](/blog/canada-pgwp-2026-guide/) for eligibility, PGWP duration, field-of-study requirements, and transition to PR.

sections.h: Education Loans for Canada: Indian Banks & Terms
sections.body:
After completing your degree in Canada, you can work in the country for up to 3 years through the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), and this work experience counts directly toward Canadian permanent residency applications. This is one of the most valuable benefits of studying in Canada�the combination of work authorization and a clear PR pathway. Unlike the USA, where you need H-1B sponsorship (which has lottery restrictions), Canadian PGWP work experience directly leads to PR through the Express Entry system in as little as 6�12 months.

The PGWP allows you to work for any Canadian employer in any field (no job list restrictions), earn CAD 50,000�80,000+ annually, and build work experience that counts toward PR. This clear pathway to permanent residency is why many Indian students choose Canada over the USA despite both countries having excellent universities. Most international students transition from PGWP to permanent residency within 5�7 years of arriving in Canada. See our complete guide: Canada PGWP 2026 Guide for eligibility, PGWP duration, field-of-study requirements, and transition to PR.

sections.h: Provinces with Lowest Cost of Living
sections.body: For budget-conscious Indian students, these provinces offer the best value:
bullets: **Quebec**: Lowest tuition (CAD 16,000–22,000/year) and lowest living costs (Montreal CAD 1,230–1,770/month)
**Atlantic Canada**: Halifax, St. John's, and other Atlantic cities offer tuition at CAD 12,000–17,000/year and living costs under CAD 1,600/month
**Alberta**: Calgary and Edmonton combine reasonable tuition (CAD 15,000–20,000/year) with affordable housing (CAD 1,450–2,000/month)
**Avoid**: Vancouver and Toronto due to high housing costs (CAD 1,200–2,000/month for rent alone)

faqs: How much does it cost to study in Canada per year?

Annual costs range from **CAD 25,000–55,000** (approximately **₹15–33 lakhs**), depending on the province and program. This includes tuition (CAD 15,000–28,000), accommodation (CAD 9,000–14,400), and living expenses (CAD 4,200–6,600).
What is the GIC requirement for a Canadian study permit?

As of 2024, **GIC requirements have been removed for most countries**, including India. However, you must still demonstrate proof of funds for tuition and living expenses. Confirm current requirements on **canada.ca** and your institution's website.
Can Indian students work part-time in Canada?

Yes, **study permit holders can work up to 20 hours/week during the academic term** and full-time during scheduled breaks. Off-campus work is permitted (unlike the USA). Typical earnings: CAD 12,000–18,000 annually.
Which Canadian province is cheapest for international students?

**Quebec and Atlantic Canada** are the most affordable. Quebec tuition is CAD 16,000–22,000/year with Montreal living costs at CAD 1,230–1,770/month. Atlantic cities (Halifax, St. John's) are even cheaper.
How long is the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) in Canada?
PGWP duration is equal to the length of your eligible study program: **up to 3 years for a 2-year master's degree**. See [Canada PGWP 2026 Guide](/blog/canada-pgwp-2026-guide/) for full details.
What is the cost difference between studying in Canada vs USA?

**Canada is 20–30% cheaper**: Canada averages CAD 30,000–50,000/year (₹18–30 lakhs) vs. USA at USD 30,000–60,000/year (₹25–48 lakhs). Additionally, Canada offers PGWP work hours and easier PR pathways.
Do I need an education loan to study in Canada?

Many Indian students use education loans to cover 70–90% of costs. Indian banks (SBI, HDFC, ICICI) offer loans at 7–10% interest with 7–15 year repayment periods. Combined with on-campus work, loans make Canada very affordable.
What is the tuition for business and engineering programs in Canada?
**Business and engineering programs cost 20–30% more** than liberal arts: typically **CAD 22,000–32,000/year** (₹13–19 lakhs) in major universities, compared to CAD 15,000–20,000 for other fields.

title: MS in USA Requirements & Costs 2026: GRE/GMAT, TOEFL, Timeline & Budget
excerpt: Complete master's degree requirements: standardized test scores (GRE/GMAT, TOEFL), GPA, SOP/LOR, application deadlines, total costs, and top universities for Indian students.
kw: MS USA requirements, GRE GMAT TOEFL 2026, MS application process, master's degree cost USA, top universities MS, timeline graduate admission

sections.h: MS in USA: Complete Application & Cost Guide for 2026
sections.body: Pursuing a Master's degree in the USA is the most popular pathway for Indian students seeking quality education and post-graduation work opportunities (OPT and H-1B visa). This guide covers all requirements, deadlines, costs, and top universities for 2026.

sections.h: Standardized Test Requirements: GRE, GMAT & TOEFL
sections.body:
Most US master's programs require standardized test scores that vary depending on your field of study. Engineering, computer science, and science graduate programs typically require the GRE (Graduate Record Examination), while MBA and business master's programs require the GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test). All international students whose native language is not English must also provide TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language) or IELTS (International English Language Testing System) scores to demonstrate English proficiency.

Test scores are submitted with your application and significantly influence admission decisions. Top 50 universities typically require higher scores (GRE 320+, GMAT 680+, TOEFL 100+), while universities ranked 50�150 often have more flexible score requirements. Some universities waived test requirements in 2024�2025 for strong profiles, though this may not continue�always check current university requirements. Preparation typically requires 3�4 months of dedicated study (300�400 hours), so plan accordingly in your application timeline.

callout.text: *Scores vary by university. Top 50 universities typically require GRE 320+, GMAT 680+, TOEFL 100+. Confirm requirements on university websites as many waived test requirements for strong profiles in 2025–2026.

sections.h: When to Start Preparing: 12-Month Application Timeline
sections.body: Plan your MS application process with this timeline:
steps: **Months 1–3 (June–August 2025)**: Research universities, identify target schools (10–15 universities across 'reach,' 'match,' and 'safety' tiers), register for GRE/GMAT/TOEFL
**Months 2–5 (July–October 2025)**: Prepare for standardized tests (GRE/GMAT: 3–4 months, TOEFL: 2–3 months), take practice exams
**Months 4–6 (September–November 2025)**: Take official GRE/GMAT/TOEFL exams, prepare SOP (Statement of Purpose) and request LORs from professors
**Months 5–7 (October–December 2025)**: Finalize applications, request transcripts, submit applications (most deadlines: December–February)
**Months 7–10 (December 2025–March 2026)**: Receive admissions decisions and scholarship offers, select university and accept offer
**Months 10–12 (March–May 2026)**: Submit visa documents (I-20), apply for F-1 visa, arrange housing

sections.h: GPA & Academic Requirements
sections.body: Most MS programs require a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0) or 7.5+ on a 10-point scale. However, competitive programs prefer GPA 3.3+.
bullets: **Minimum GPA**: 3.0/4.0 (7.5/10) for most universities
**Competitive GPA**: 3.3–3.8/4.0 (8.5+/10) for top 50 universities
**Transcripts**: Request official transcripts from your undergraduate institution; most programs require sealed official copies
**Additional courses**: If GPA is below 3.0, consider post-graduate certificates or online courses (Coursera, edX) to strengthen profile

sections.h: Statement of Purpose (SOP) & Letters of Recommendation (LOR)
sections.body: SOP and LORs are critical for admission decisions, especially if test scores are borderline. Most programs require 2–3 LORs and a 250–500 word SOP.
bullets: **SOP**: Explain your academic background, career goals, why this specific program and university, research interests if applicable
**LORs**: Ideally 2–3 letters from professors or research mentors who can speak to your academic capabilities
**Timing**: Request LORs 4–6 weeks before application deadlines to give recommenders sufficient time
**Online submission**: Most universities use application portals (Common App, Naviance, or university-specific systems) to collect LORs directly from referees

sections.h: Application Fees, Visa & Documentation Costs
sections.body:
Beyond standardized test fees, you'll incur significant costs for applications, visa processing, and documentation. Most universities charge between USD 60�80 per application, and students typically apply to 10�15 universities (creating a USD 600�1,200 cost). Add US government visa fees, medical exams, and document processing, and total non-tuition costs reach USD 2,000�3,000 before you even begin studying.

Factor in international wire transfer fees, courier services for physical documents, and travel to visa appointments (if conducted in India). Some universities offer fee waivers for students with financial need�reach out to the admissions office after submitting your profile to inquire about eligibility. Additionally, budget USD 2,000�3,000 for initial accommodation deposit, furniture, and setting up utilities when you arrive in the USA. Many students overlook these first-month costs and run short of funds upon arrival.

sections.h: Total Cost of MS in USA: 2-Year Budget
sections.body: A 2-year master's degree in the USA typically costs USD 60,000–150,000 total. Here's a realistic breakdown:

callout.text: **Private universities cost 30–50% more**: expect USD 140,000–200,000 for 2 years. Many students work on-campus (USD 10,000–15,000/year) and use scholarships (USD 5,000–25,000/year) to reduce costs significantly.

sections.h: Top MS Universities for Indian Students 2026
sections.body: These universities consistently rank well, offer strong funding to international students, and have large Indian student communities:
bullets: **Tier 1 (Top 20)**: MIT, Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, Georgia Tech, University of Illinois—highest selectivity, limited scholarships but strong OPT outcomes
**Tier 2 (Top 50)**: Penn State, Ohio State, University of Michigan, Purdue, UC San Diego, Virginia Tech, Michigan State—good funding, strong programs
**Tier 3 (50–100)**: Arizona State, University of Texas—Dallas, University of Florida, Northeastern—generous funding, easier admission, strong job placement
**STEM leaders**: MIT, CMU, Stanford for CS/AI; Georgia Tech, UT Austin for engineering; Wharton, Columbia for MBA

sections.h: Scholarships & Financial Aid for International Students
sections.body: Many universities offer merit-based scholarships to international students. Apply strategically to maximize aid.
bullets: **University scholarships**: Most top 50 universities offer merit scholarships ranging from $5,000–25,000/year
**Need-based aid**: Limited for international students; some universities (MIT, CMU) have need-blind admission and meet 100% of demonstrated need
**External scholarships**: Fulbright, Inlaks Scholarships, ICCR fellowships (highly competitive)
**Assistantships**: Teaching assistantships (TA) and research assistantships (RA) cover tuition + USD 12,000–18,000 stipend/year (very competitive)

sections.h: Post-MS: OPT, H-1B & Permanent Residency Pathway
sections.body:
MS graduates can work in the USA for up to 12 months (24 months for STEM degrees) on Optional Practical Training (OPT). After OPT, many transition to H-1B visa for longer employment.

See [USA OPT STEM Extension 2026 Guide](/blog/usa-opt-stem-extension-2026-guide/) for detailed eligibility, timeline, and H-1B sponsorship.

faqs: What are the requirements for an MS in the USA?

Main requirements: (1) **GRE or GMAT** score (varies by program), (2) **TOEFL/IELTS** score (90+ TOEFL for most universities), (3) **Bachelor's degree with minimum GPA 3.0/4.0**, (4) **SOP and 2–3 LORs**, (5) **Valid passport**.
What GRE and TOEFL scores are needed for MS admission?

**GRE**: Competitive score is 320–330 out of 340. **TOEFL**: 90–100 out of 120 for top 50 universities. Requirements vary; many universities waived test requirements for strong profiles in 2025–2026. Check university-specific requirements.
How long should I prepare for GRE and TOEFL exams?
**GRE preparation**: 3–4 months (300–400 hours of study). **TOEFL preparation**: 2–3 months (150–250 hours). Start 6–8 months before application deadlines to allow time for retakes if needed.
How much does an MS in the USA cost?
**Total 2-year cost**: USD 90,000–145,000 (₹72–116 lakhs). Public universities cost USD 50,000–80,000 tuition + USD 30,000–50,000 living expenses. Private universities cost 30–50% more.
When are MS application deadlines in the USA?
Most MS deadlines are **December to February** for Fall 2026 admission. Some universities have rolling admissions. Early submission (by October–November) increases scholarship chances.
Can I get a scholarship for MS in the USA?

Yes, many universities offer merit scholarships ranging from **$5,000–25,000/year**. Top universities (MIT, CMU) offer need-blind aid for all students. Research assistantships (RA) and teaching assistantships (TA) cover tuition + stipend.
What is the difference between GRE and GMAT for MS programs?

**GRE** is for most master's programs (engineering, science, analytics). **GMAT** is primarily for MBA and business master's programs. Some universities accept either. Choose based on your target program.
How long is an MS degree in the USA?
Standard MS degrees are **2 years (4 semesters)** full-time. Some programs are 1.5 years or 3 years depending on coursework and thesis requirements. Confirm duration with your university.

title: Canada PGWP 2026: Eligibility, Duration, Field-of-Study Rules & Application Guide
excerpt: Complete PGWP guide for Indian graduates: eligibility requirements, PGWP duration by program length (up to 3 years), field-of-study rules, language requirements, and step-by-step application process.
kw: Canada PGWP 2026, post-graduation work permit, PGWP eligibility, PGWP duration, field of study requirement, PGWP application

sections.h: Canada Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) 2026: Complete Guide
sections.body:
The Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) is one of the most valuable benefits of studying in Canada. It allows graduates to work legally in Canada for up to 3 years after graduation, and this work experience directly counts toward Canadian permanent residency (PR) applications.

PGWP is a critical pathway for Indian students to transition from study to work to PR in Canada.

sections.h: Who is Eligible for PGWP in 2026?
sections.body: To be eligible for a PGWP, you must meet ALL of the following criteria:
bullets: **Study in Canada**: Completed a full-time program (minimum 8 months) at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) in Canada
**Valid study permit**: Held a valid study permit while studying and while applying for PGWP
**Completed studies**: Successfully graduated with a diploma or degree (confirmation from institution)
**Program length**: Studied for a minimum of 8 months in a program designated as PGWP-eligible
**Time limit**: Apply within 180 days of graduation or after receiving proof of graduation—whichever comes first

callout.text: **180-day application window**: You MUST apply for PGWP within 180 days of receiving your graduation document. Missing this deadline means losing PGWP eligibility permanently.

sections.h: PGWP Eligibility by Program Type & Duration
sections.body: PGWP duration depends on the length of your study program. Not all programs qualify for PGWP—the program must be eligible and meet minimum requirements.

sections.h: Field-of-Study Requirement: Which Programs are PGWP-Eligible?
sections.body:
As of 2024, a major change: **PGWP is limited to graduates from programs in priority fields**. The government restricts PGWP to healthcare, skilled trades, and technology.

**Note**: Rules are changing for 2026–2027. Verify current eligible fields on **canada.ca** before enrolling.
bullets: **GENERALLY eligible programs**: Healthcare (nursing, medicine, therapy), STEM (engineering, computer science, mathematics), skilled trades (plumbing, welding, construction)
**Often restricted (confirm)**: Business administration, hospitality, social sciences without STEM focus, pure liberal arts
**Eligible institution status**: Your university must be on Canada's **Designated Learning Institution (DLI) list**—most Canadian universities are DLI; international branch campuses may not be
**PGWP eligibility confirmation**: Contact your institution's international office BEFORE enrolling to confirm your program qualifies for PGWP

callout.text: **2024–2026 policy changes**: Canada has restricted PGWP to priority fields to address labor shortages. Rules have changed and may continue to evolve. Always confirm with your institution and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) before committing to a program.

sections.h: Language Requirements for PGWP Application
sections.body: PGWP applications do NOT require a separate English/French language test score. However, if you took your studies in a language other than English or French, IRCC may request evidence that you completed the program in that language.
bullets: **If you studied in English or French**: No language requirement for PGWP—submit graduation documents
**If you studied in another language**: Provide official translation of diploma/degree (notarized English translation), plus evidence from institution that instruction was in that language
**Bilingual programs**: No additional language test required

sections.h: Step-by-Step PGWP Application Process
sections.body: Follow this process to apply for your PGWP within 180 days of graduation:
steps: **Step 1**: Obtain official graduation confirmation from your institution (typically provided with your diploma or available from the registrar)
**Step 2**: Gather required documents: valid passport, study permit, proof of graduation, proof of identity, proof of residence in Canada (if applicable)
**Step 3**: Create/log into your **Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) account** at **canada.ca**
**Step 4**: Select 'Apply for Post-Graduation Work Permit' from the application options
**Step 5**: Complete the online application form with personal details, study program info, institution name, graduation date
**Step 6**: Upload all required documents (passport, study permit, graduation letter, notarized translations if needed)
**Step 7**: Pay the application fee: **CAD 255** (non-refundable)
**Step 8**: Submit application online and receive confirmation email with your application reference number
**Step 9**: Wait for processing (typically 4–6 weeks for online applications, 8–12 weeks for paper applications) and receive decision via IRCC portal or email

sections.h: PGWP Document Checklist
sections.body: Ensure you have all required documents before applying to avoid delays or rejection:

rows: Official letter from institution on letterhead
Must state completion date and program name
Must be valid for PGWP duration (ideally 3+ years)
Copy of study permit confirmation of permanent residence or TRN (Temporary Resident Number)
Required to prove you were authorized to study
Birth certificate or national identity card
Utility bill, lease, or official mail dated within 3 months

sections.h: PGWP Duration & Work Restrictions
sections.body: PGWP is typically valid for the same duration as your study program (up to 3 years maximum). However, it is **NOT employer-specific**—you can work for any employer in Canada.
bullets: **PGWP duration**: Equal to program length (minimum 1 year, maximum 3 years)
**Employer flexibility**: Work for any Canadian employer—can change jobs without notifying IRCC
**Geographic flexibility**: Work anywhere in Canada (no provincial restrictions)
**Self-employment**: PGWP permits self-employment and starting your own business
**Part-time and full-time**: Can work full-time, part-time, or multiple jobs simultaneously
**Extensions**: PGWP cannot be extended once expired—if you need to stay, apply for PR or another visa category before expiration

sections.h: Transitioning from PGWP to Canadian Permanent Residency (PR)
sections.body:
The key advantage of PGWP is that the work experience earned **counts directly toward PR applications through Express Entry**.

**Common pathway:**
1. Graduate and obtain PGWP (work permit valid 1–3 years)
2. Work in a skilled occupation for 12–24 months (work experience qualifies you for Canadian Experience Class)
3. Apply for PR through Express Entry (your PGWP work experience + Canadian qualifications → higher points → faster approval)
4. Receive PR decision (typically 6 months)
5. Transition to Permanent Residency (PR), then citizenship after 3 years

See [USA OPT STEM Extension 2026 Guide](/blog/usa-opt-stem-extension-2026-guide/) for comparison with USA OPT work permits.

callout.text: **PGWP = Express Entry fast-track**: Work experience on PGWP directly counts toward Canadian Experience Class (CEC), which typically processes PR applications in 6 months. This is faster than many other PR pathways.

sections.h: Common PGWP Application Issues & Solutions
sections.body: Avoid these common mistakes when applying:
bullets: **Missing the 180-day deadline**: Mark your graduation date + 180 days on a calendar; apply 30–60 days early to avoid missing the deadline
**Incorrect institution name**: Double-check your institution's exact legal name on the DLI list; using a nickname or common name may cause rejection
**Non-DLI institution**: Confirm your university is on the DLI list before enrolling. Graduates of non-DLI institutions are NOT eligible for PGWP
**Incomplete application**: Submit ALL required documents in one package; incomplete applications are returned and delay processing by weeks
**Language issues**: If your degree was in a non-English/French language, obtain a notarized translation of your diploma AND written confirmation from your institution

faqs: What is the PGWP duration for 2026?

**PGWP duration equals your program length**: A 2-year master's degree qualifies for a **3-year PGWP** (maximum). Shorter programs (8 months–1 year) qualify for PGWP up to that program duration. Maximum PGWP is **3 years**.
Am I eligible for PGWP if I studied online or outside Canada?

**No**, PGWP requires you to study in Canada at a **Designated Learning Institution (DLI)**. Online programs delivered by Canadian institutions may qualify, but international branch campuses often do NOT. Confirm eligibility with your institution.
Can I apply for PGWP if my study permit expired?

You must have held a valid study permit **while studying**. If your permit expires after graduation but before your PGWP application, you can still apply within 180 days. Restore status online if permit expired (apply from within Canada).
What is the 180-day deadline for PGWP applications?

You MUST apply for PGWP within **180 days of receiving your graduation document** (diploma, degree, or official graduation letter). Missing this deadline permanently disqualifies you—extensions are NOT granted.
Can I work anywhere in Canada on PGWP?
Yes, PGWP allows you to work **anywhere in Canada, for any employer, full-time or part-time**. You can change employers without notifying IRCC or reporting. No provincial restrictions.
Does PGWP require a specific job offer?

No, PGWP does NOT require a job offer. You can apply immediately after graduation and search for a job during the PGWP validity period. However, some employers prefer applicants with PGWP already in hand.
How does PGWP lead to permanent residency in Canada?
Work experience on PGWP counts toward the **Canadian Experience Class (CEC)** in Express Entry. After 12–24 months of skilled work on PGWP, you can apply for PR, which processes in ~6 months.
Is PGWP available for all Canadian degree programs?

No, PGWP is restricted to **priority fields** as of 2024: healthcare, STEM, and skilled trades. Business administration, hospitality, and non-STEM programs may not qualify. Confirm with your institution before enrolling.

title: USA OPT & STEM Extension 2026: 12-Month Base + 24-Month STEM, Timeline & H-1B Path
excerpt: Complete OPT guide for F-1 graduates: 12-month Optional Practical Training, 24-month STEM extension eligibility, employer E-Verify requirements, H-1B visa transition, and cap-gap work authorization.
kw: USA OPT 2026, STEM extension 24 months, F-1 visa OPT, Optional Practical Training, H-1B sponsorship, OPT cap-gap, E-Verify requirement

sections.h: USA Optional Practical Training (OPT) & STEM Extension 2026: Complete Guide
sections.body:
Optional Practical Training (OPT) allows F-1 visa graduates to work legally in the USA for 12 months after graduation. International students in STEM fields (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) qualify for an additional 24-month extension, totaling up to 36 months of work authorization.

OPT is the primary pathway for Indian graduates to transition from student status to employment-based immigration (H-1B, EB-3, L-1 visas).

sections.h: Who Qualifies for OPT in 2026?
sections.body: You are eligible for OPT if you meet all of the following criteria:
bullets: **Current or recent F-1 visa holder**: Maintain or recently maintained F-1 status while studying
**Completed program**: Graduated with a degree (bachelor's, master's, or doctorate) or completed a full academic year and maintain F-1 status
**USCIS authorization**: Your degree was completed within the past 60 days (new 2024 rule; previously 12 months), OR you maintain valid F-1 status
**STEM vs. Non-STEM**: All F-1 graduates qualify for 12-month OPT; STEM graduates qualify for an additional 24-month extension
**Employment intent**: Plan to work in a position related to your field of study

callout.text: **2024 policy update**: USCIS tightened OPT eligibility—you must apply within **60 days of graduation** if you've left the USA. If you're still in the US on F-1 status, you have more flexibility. Confirm current rules on USCIS.gov.

sections.h: OPT Duration: Base 12 Months + STEM Extension Up to 24 Months
sections.body: OPT work authorization is split into two phases:
bullets: **Initial 12-month OPT**: Available to all F-1 graduates in any field; must be related to field of study
**STEM Extension (24 months)**: Available only if your degree is in a STEM field listed by USCIS; adds 24 additional months for total of 36 months
**Gap in employment**: You can have up to 90 days of unemployment total on OPT; any time over 90 days may violate your OPT and require repatriation
**Multiple OPT periods**: Can have pre-completion OPT (before graduation, 1 month max) and post-completion OPT (12 months after graduation)

sections.h: STEM Fields & OPT Extension Eligibility
sections.body: STEM Extension eligibility is based on your **degree major, NOT your job title**. Check if your degree qualifies for STEM extension:
bullets: **STEM degree examples**: Computer Science, Engineering (all types), Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Data Science, Cyber Security, Information Security
**Borderline fields** (check USCIS list): Business with CS focus, Finance with quant focus—only qualify if your specific degree is STEM-listed
**Non-STEM degrees** (no extension): Business Administration, MBA, Liberal Arts, Social Sciences, Economics, Law, most humanities
**Verification**: Search USCIS's official STEM degree list on **uscis.gov** using your exact degree name; if unsure, consult your university's international student office

sections.h: OPT Application Process: Step-by-Step Timeline
sections.body: Apply for OPT 120–90 days before your program end date to avoid employment gaps:
steps: **Step 1** (120–90 days before graduation): Obtain official recommendation letter from your university's international student office (OPT recommendation)
**Step 2**: Complete the **Form I-765** (Application for Employment Authorization Document) available on USCIS.gov
**Step 3**: Gather required documents: Form I-765, passport photocopy, copy of F-1 visa or I-94 record, university OPT recommendation letter, recent passport photo
**Step 4**: Calculate the fee: **$410** (as of 2026; confirm on USCIS.gov). Make payable to 'U.S. Department of Homeland Security'
**Step 5**: Choose filing location: mail to your **designated USCIS service center** (based on your university location) or use **USCIS online filing portal** (ELIS) if available in your jurisdiction
**Step 6**: Track application status on **USCIS.gov** using your receipt number (sent to you after submission)
**Step 7**: Receive Employment Authorization Document (EAD/OPT card) in mail (typically 2–4 months; expedited processing available for additional fee)
**Step 8**: Begin employment within 60 days of EAD receipt. Employer must verify your authorization via E-Verify system

callout.text: **Processing delays**: OPT approval can take 2–4 months (sometimes 6+ months if additional evidence requested). Apply as early as possible—120 days before graduation—to avoid employment start delays.

sections.h: E-Verify Requirement & Employer Responsibility
sections.body: All employers sponsoring OPT employees must verify work authorization through **E-Verify**, the federal system that confirms you're authorized to work in the USA.
bullets: **E-Verify**: Your employer submits your I-9 documents to E-Verify within 3 days of hire. System verifies your name, birth date, Social Security Number against government databases
**Employer compliance**: Most US employers use E-Verify; if they don't, they must use **Form I-9** verification but are not compliant with federal regulations
**Your responsibility**: Ensure employer has your correct legal name, birth date, passport number, and Social Security Number (obtain an ITIN from IRS if needed)
**E-Verify matches**: 99% of OPT employees pass E-Verify on first try. If there's a mismatch, work with your employer and USCIS to resolve it within 8 business days

sections.h: OPT Cap-Gap & H-1B Bridge Visa
sections.body: If your OPT expires before your H-1B visa begins (typically October 1), you can work on **cap-gap** authority—transitional work authorization while awaiting H-1B approval.
bullets: **Cap-Gap eligibility**: You must have an H-1B petition filed by April 1 for October 1 H-1B start date
**Gap period**: OPT typically expires 12 months after start date. If H-1B lottery doesn't select you until July–August, you have a 2–3 month gap
**Cap-Gap authorization**: USCIS grants automatic extension on your current EAD (same OPT card) through the H-1B start date (October 1)
**No action required**: Cap-Gap is automatic if H-1B petition is pending; no additional application needed
**Employer continuation**: Continue working for the same employer or switch employers if new employer files an H-1B petition before your OPT expiration

sections.h: Transitioning from OPT to H-1B Visa Sponsorship
sections.body:
After OPT, most Indian graduates transition to H-1B visa sponsorship for continued employment in the USA. H-1B is an employment-based visa valid for 3 years (extendable to 6 years).

**OPT → H-1B timeline:**
- **Year 1 (OPT)**: Work on initial 12-month OPT, gain US work experience
- **STEM Extension (optional)**: Apply for 24-month STEM extension if eligible; work until year 3
- **H-1B filing window**: Employer files H-1B petition in March–April for October 1 start date
- **H-1B approval**: USCIS processes petition by September; cap-gap bridges any gap until October
- **H-1B visa stamp**: Consular processing in India or visa interview (if outside USA) for H-1B visa stamp

See our guide on [H-1B visa sponsorship and immigration timeline] for detailed H-1B process.

sections.h: Maintaining F-1 Status While on OPT
sections.body: While working on OPT, you must maintain compliance with F-1 visa requirements to preserve your status and H-1B eligibility:
bullets: **Valid passport**: Keep your passport valid throughout OPT (recommended to have 6+ months validity beyond OPT end date)
**I-20 document**: Maintain your I-20 from your university (even while on OPT); some employers require it for employment verification
**Address reporting**: Update SEVP (Student and Exchange Visitor Program) with any address changes within 10 days
**No breaking the law**: Any criminal conviction, overstay, or unauthorized employment voids your F-1 status and disqualifies you from H-1B sponsorship
**Return/transfer**: If you leave the USA before OPT expires, you may lose remaining OPT authorization; confirm with your DSO (Designated School Official) before departing

sections.body: Here's the financial and timeline breakdown for OPT:

faqs: What is OPT for F-1 students in the USA?

**OPT (Optional Practical Training)** is work authorization for F-1 graduates to work in the USA for 12 months after graduation. STEM graduates can extend for an additional 24 months (total 36 months).
How long can I work on OPT in the USA?
**12 months of initial OPT** for all F-1 graduates. **STEM graduates: up to 36 months total** (12 months initial + 24-month extension). Non-STEM graduates are limited to 12 months with no extension.
What is the STEM extension for OPT?

STEM extension is an **additional 24-month work authorization** available only to graduates in STEM fields (Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, etc.). Eligibility is based on your degree major, not your job title.
How do I apply for OPT?

File **Form I-765 (Application for Employment Authorization Document)** with USCIS 120–90 days before graduation. Fee is **$410**. Processing takes 2–4 months. Submit with university OPT recommendation letter.
Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
No, OPT does NOT require a job offer. You can apply immediately after graduation and search for a job during OPT validity. However, your job must be related to your field of study.
What is cap-gap and how does it work?

**Cap-gap** is automatic work authorization extension while your H-1B visa petition is pending. If your OPT expires before H-1B approval (July–September), USCIS automatically extends your EAD through October 1 H-1B start date.
Do employers need to do E-Verify for OPT employees?

Yes, employers **must verify your work authorization through E-Verify** within 3 days of hire. Most US employers use E-Verify; they submit your I-9 documents, and the system confirms you're authorized to work.
Can I change employers while on OPT?

Yes, you can **change employers anytime on OPT** with no restrictions. Your OPT authorization is not tied to a single employer (unlike H-1B, which is employer-specific). New employer must complete E-Verify.

title: UK Graduate Route Visa 2026: 2–3 Year Post-Study Work Permit, Dependants & Skilled Worker Path
excerpt: Complete UK Graduate Route guide: 2-year work authorization (3 years for PhD), eligibility requirements, dependent rules 2024+, no salary threshold, and transition to Skilled Worker visa.
kw: UK Graduate Route 2026, post-study work permit, Graduate Route visa eligibility, dependent rules UK, Skilled Worker visa transition

sections.h: UK Graduate Route Visa 2026: Work Authorization for International Students
sections.body:
The UK Graduate Route allows international students to stay and work in the UK for up to 2 years after graduation (3 years for PhD graduates) without requiring a job offer or sponsorship. This is one of the most generous post-study work permits globally, allowing graduates to search for jobs, work for any employer, or start a business.

The Graduate Route is available to all eligible graduates, regardless of salary threshold or job field.

sections.h: Who Qualifies for the UK Graduate Route in 2026?
sections.body: To be eligible for the Graduate Route, you must meet ALL of the following criteria:
bullets: **Student visa holder**: Held a valid UK Student visa (or Isle of Man, Jersey, or Guernsey student visa) while studying
**Completed degree**: Successfully completed a degree program at an approved UK institution (bachelor's, master's, or doctorate)
**RQF Level 6+**: Degree must be at UK Qualification Framework Level 6 or above (typically bachelor's degree or higher)
**Application timing**: Apply for Graduate Route within 2 weeks of graduation OR while still in valid student visa status (before visa expiration)
**No criminal conviction**: Not subject to deportation; no serious criminal record
**English language requirement**: Already met while studying; no separate TOEFL/IELTS required

callout.text: **No job offer required**: Unlike other countries, the UK Graduate Route requires NO job offer, salary threshold, or employer sponsorship. You can search for jobs while in the UK.

sections.h: Graduate Route Duration: 2 Years (3 Years for PhD)
sections.body: Graduate Route validity depends on your degree level:
bullets: **2-year Graduate Route**: For all undergraduate and master's degrees (bachelor's, MSc, MA, MBA, etc.)
**3-year Graduate Route**: For PhD and doctoral research degrees only
**Full-time or part-time work**: Work any hours—no restrictions like student visa (max 20 hours/week study requirement)
**Self-employment**: Start your own business, freelance work allowed
**Job switching**: Change employers unlimited times; no sponsorship or visa application required

sections.h: Graduate Route Work Restrictions Lifted (2024 Update)
sections.body: As of 2024, the UK removed salary thresholds and job list restrictions for Graduate Route holders—you can now work in ANY job role, not just shortage occupations.
bullets: **No salary minimum**: Previously required £20,800+ salary for some routes; no longer applies to Graduate Route
**All occupations eligible**: Can work as retail assistant, waiter, nurse, engineer, IT professional—any UK job
**No job list requirement**: Not limited to 'Shortage Occupation List' or specific sectors
**Self-employment**: Run your own business (sole proprietor, limited company, partnership)
**Freelancing**: Work as independent contractor for multiple clients simultaneously

sections.h: Bringing Dependants on the Graduate Route (2024 Changes)
sections.body: As of 2024, dependent spouse/partner and children rules for Graduate Route have been tightened. Eligibility is very limited:

rows: Only if married BEFORE arriving for studies
Limited—must have existed before student visa
Cohabitation must predate student visa by 2+ years
Only if had custody before arriving for studies

callout.text: **2024 dependent restrictions**: The UK significantly tightened dependent eligibility on Graduate Route. If you're married or have children after arriving in the UK, they cannot join you on your Graduate Route visa. Dependants must have already been dependants before you applied for your student visa.

sections.h: Graduate Route Visa Application Process
sections.body: Apply for Graduate Route within 2 weeks of graduating or while in valid student status:
steps: **Step 1**: Obtain confirmation of graduation from your university (transcript or graduation letter with date and degree details)
**Step 2**: Check your eligibility: degree level RQF 6+, valid student visa at time of application
**Step 3**: Visit **UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) portal** on gov.uk and create account or log in
**Step 4**: Select 'Apply for Graduate Route' visa in the portal; choose 'Inside the UK' application (if still in UK) or 'Outside the UK' (if departed)
**Step 5**: Complete online application form: personal details, passport info, university details, graduation date, dependant information if any
**Step 6**: Upload required documents: valid passport, graduation transcript/letter, current student visa/BRP (Biometric Residence Permit), proof of address in UK
**Step 7**: Pay application fee: **£719** (as of 2026; includes Immigration Health Surcharge [IHS] of approximately £284/year)
**Step 8**: Submit application and receive confirmation with transaction ID
**Step 9**: Wait for decision (typically 4–8 weeks if applying from UK; 8–12 weeks from outside UK)
**Step 10**: Receive Graduate Route visa letter and new BRP in post (if in UK) or visa vignette in passport (if applied from abroad)

sections.h: Graduate Route Document Checklist
sections.body: Gather all required documents before applying to avoid rejection or delays:

rows: Original—must be valid for at least 6 months beyond Graduate Route end date
Official letter from university with degree name, date conferred, and RQF level
Must state you successfully completed the degree
Copy of current valid student visa in passport or BRP card
Proof you held student status during graduation
Utility bill, council tax, or official mail dated within 3 months
Official transcript showing degree awarded and grades (optional but recommended)
Strengthens application if degree not recently conferred

sections.h: Work Rights & Restrictions on Graduate Route
sections.body: Once you receive your Graduate Route visa, you have extensive work freedoms:
bullets: **Unlimited hours**: Work full-time, part-time, multiple jobs simultaneously
**Any employer**: No sponsorship required; work for any UK employer without visa application
**Job switching**: Change employers anytime with no notification to UKVI
**Self-employment**: Register as sole trader, start limited company, or freelance work
**Sector flexibility**: Work in any industry—no restrictions based on job list or shortage occupations
**Remote work**: Can work remotely for UK employers or international companies while in UK
**Study**: Can study full-time or part-time while working on Graduate Route (no work restrictions like student visa)

sections.h: Transitioning from Graduate Route to Skilled Worker Visa
sections.body: The **Skilled Worker visa** is the primary pathway from Graduate Route to permanent residency (PR) in the UK. Many graduates transition from Graduate Route (2–3 years work) to Skilled Worker sponsorship.
bullets: **Skilled Worker visa requirements**: Job offer from UK employer, salary of at least £26,200 (or higher for specific roles), employer sponsorship license
**Timeline**: Search for Skilled Worker sponsor employer during your 2-year Graduate Route period; once you have an offer and sponsorship, apply for Skilled Worker visa
**Continuous residence**: Time on Graduate Route counts toward Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR/PR) if you transition to Skilled Worker within allowed timeframe
**ILR pathway**: 5 years in UK on work visas → eligible for Indefinite Leave to Remain (PR); 6 years → eligible for British citizenship
**Salary requirement**: Entry-level salary is £26,200+; specialist roles have higher requirements. Check your job role on Skilled Worker list

callout.text: **Graduate Route → Skilled Worker → PR timeline**: Year 0–2: Graduate Route work. Year 2–5: Skilled Worker visa sponsorship. Year 5: Apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain (PR). Year 6: Apply for British citizenship.

faqs: What is the UK Graduate Route visa duration in 2026?

**2 years** for bachelor's and master's degrees. **3 years** for PhD or other doctorate degrees. No extension available—you must transition to another visa category (Skilled Worker, Spouse) after expiration.
Do I need a job offer to apply for the Graduate Route?
**No**, the Graduate Route requires NO job offer, sponsorship, or salary threshold. You can apply immediately after graduation and search for jobs while in the UK.
Can I work any job on the Graduate Route visa?
Yes, **any UK job is permitted**—no salary minimum, no job list restrictions. You can work as retail assistant, nurse, engineer, IT professional, or start your own business. Completely flexible.
Can I bring my spouse/dependants on the Graduate Route?
**Very limited**. Only dependants who were already dependants BEFORE you arrived for your student visa can join. Spouses married after arriving cannot join. Confirm specific rules with UKVI.
How much does the Graduate Route cost?
**£719** total (approx. USD 900 or ₹75,000) including the application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS). IHS gives you access to UK NHS healthcare.
When should I apply for the Graduate Route?
Apply **within 2 weeks of graduation** or **while you still have valid student visa status**. Applying after your student visa expires may disqualify you or require separate immigration application.
What happens after my 2-year Graduate Route expires?

After expiration, you must transition to another visa: **Skilled Worker** (job sponsorship, PR pathway), **Spouse visa** (marriage), **Innovator/Start-Up visa** (business), or **Student visa** (further study). No extensions available.
How does Graduate Route lead to UK permanent residency?

Graduate Route alone does NOT lead to PR. You must transition to **Skilled Worker visa** with employer sponsorship (5 years total needed). After 5 years continuous UK residence on work visas, you're eligible for **Indefinite Leave to Remain (PR)**.
